parsed.summary: `not_erdos_146` proves that Erdős's degeneracy conjecture fails. The conjecture is stated as: every bipartite r-degenerate graph H with r > 0 satisfies ex(n,H) = O(n^{2-1/r}). This faithfully captures the consequence of Theorem 1.2. The single most important caveat is in `twoDegenerateExtremalCounterexample`: it quantifies universally (∀ q H) where the paper's Theorem 1.2 is existential (∃ H). As written it asserts that every graph on Fin q is connected, bipartite, 2-degenerate, and has extremal number ≥ c n^{3/2+ε}, which is false (e.g. q = 0). So it does not state Theorem 1.2. Theorem 1.1 is not formalized.

glossary.plain: N_G(v) ∩ s: the neighbours of v lying in the finite set s
Every nonempty finite vertex set s contains a vertex v with |N(v) ∩ s| ≤ r
glossary.note: Uses induced subgraphs rather than arbitrary subgraphs. This is equivalent, since deleting edges only lowers degrees.

glossary.plain: For all r > 0 and every bipartite r-degenerate graph H on Fin q: ex(n,H) = O(n^{2-1/r}) as n → ∞
glossary.note: Uses Mathlib extremalNumber (non-induced subgraph containment) and IsBigO atTop. The cast ((2:ℕ):ℝ) - 1/(r:ℝ) is correct for r > 0.

lean_claims.plain: For EVERY q ∈ ℕ and EVERY simple graph H on Fin q, all of the following hold: (a) H is connected, bipartite and 2-degenerate; (b) for every proper 2-colouring and each colour class, the max degree in that class is > 2; (c) there exist c, ε > 0 with c·n^{3/2+ε} ≤ ex(n,H) for all large n.
There exist r > 0, q, and a bipartite r-degenerate graph H on Fin q such that ex(n,H) is not O(n^{2-1/r}).

paper_claims.plain: There is a finite nonempty family F of connected bipartite graphs, each containing a cycle, with ex(n,F) = O(n^{4/3-1/48}) but ex(n,F) = Ω(n^{4/3}) for each F ∈ F.
There exist a fixed connected bipartite 2-degenerate graph H and constants c, ε > 0 with ex(n,H) ≥ c n^{3/2+ε} for all sufficiently large n.
Erdős's conjecture that every bipartite r-degenerate graph has ex(n,H) = O(n^{2-1/r}) is false (already for r = 2).

coverage.why: No statement about the compactness conjecture or families.
Universal ∀ q H instead of existential ∃ q H; the Lean statement is false.
Negation of conjecture (3), which follows from Theorem 1.2 since n^{3/2+ε} is not O(n^{3/2}).

flags.explanation: The statement begins `∀ (q : ℕ) (H : SimpleGraph (Fin q)), H.Connected ∧ ...`, but the paper asserts existence of such an H. As written it claims every graph is connected, bipartite, 2-degenerate, etc. That is false: for q = 0, Fin 0 is empty and so not Connected. Also, the complete graph on Fin 3 is not bipartite. So the theorem does not formalize Theorem 1.2, and if it were genuinely proved the environment would be inconsistent.
flags.probe_idea: theorem probe : ¬ (∀ (q : ℕ) (H : SimpleGraph (Fin q)), H.Connected) := fun h => (h 0 ⊥).nonempty.elim (fun x => x.elim0)

flags.explanation: There is an extra conjunct: every colour class of every proper 2-colouring has max degree > 2. Since Finset.sup over an empty class is 0, this also forces both classes to be nonempty. It is not in the paper's Theorem 1.2 statement, though plausibly true of the paper's H (it rules out the known Füredi/AKS case). In an existential reading this would only strengthen the claim.
The compactness counterexample (Theorem 1.1) is not formalized anywhere.
